item.statement: For any one-hidden-layer nu-homogeneous network, any width, 2<=b<=nu: gamma*_b <= C_b^{nu/b} Gamma_{nu/b}(p)
item.what_to_check: Core result; search for L_{2,b} (b != nu, esp. weight decay b=2) max-margin analyses of modular addition: Morwani, Li et al. 2025, Tian 2024 algebraic objects, Jacobs-Montufar, AdamW/l_inf margin papers

chk.evidence:
The b = nu endpoint is known. Morwani et al., ICLR 2024 (arXiv 2311.07568; I fetched the HTML) prove all their theorems only at L_{2,nu}. Their Thm 7 gives the max L_{2,3} margin as sqrt(2/27)/(p^{1/2}(p-1)) for the quadratic net with width >= 4(p-1). Plain L2 appears only empirically: Fig 4b says L2 ReLU neurons are "nearly 1-sparse ... but not quite". Li, Liang, Shi, Song and Zhou, AISTATS 2025, PMLR 258:523-531 (proceedings page fetched) state only a maximum L_{2,k+1} margin, with m >= 2^{2k-2}(p-1). Our cor:dense reproduces Morwani Thm 7, and the paper already says so.

The b < nu case, including b = 2 weight decay, was not found anywhere. Papers I checked:
- Mohamadi et al., ICML 2024 (2407.12332, HTML): the norm is l_inf. Prop 3.8 only shows that zero-loss solutions exist with ||theta||_inf <= floor(h/8p)^{-1/3}; Thm 4.5 is a generalisation bound for Omega(p) margin. There is no upper bound on the max margin over all widths.
- Tian, NeurIPS 2025 (2410.01779): Thm 5 says "lower-order solutions are preferred if trained with L2 regularization", argued by path-connectivity. There is no margin bound.
- Jacobs and Montufar 2026 (2605.19458): mirror flow. No modular addition and no L_{2,b} bound.
- Kam, Bessafi and Cadet 2026 (2609.17926, HTML App. A.3.2): Eq 15 is max over ||beta||_2 = B of min_s sum_k beta_k(1-cos(omega_k s)), and Prop 5 finds a uniform allocation optimal. The l2 budget on the amplitudes is posited for the quadratic net only; it is not derived from homogeneity, and they make no claim for all networks or widths. This is the closest analogue of the coverage programme, but not of the universal bound.
- Memana 2026 (2608.04451) and Nguyen 2026 (2606.17399) are irrelevant.

The pricing step (amplitude A costs A^{b/nu}, then subadditivity) is a known ingredient:
- Hoff (arXiv 1611.00040): "a subclass of L_q penalties with q<=1 can be expressed as sums of L_2 penalties".
- Dai, Karzand and Srebro, NeurIPS 2021: the representation cost of l2 regularisation on the parameters.
- Fan, Ding, Yang, Zhang and Udell, TMLR 2023 (2012.03436): regularisers built from the Euclidean norms of CP components are "monotonic transformations of tensor Schatten-p quasi-norm". A product neuron is a rank-one CP term, so our pricing is the diagonal (Fourier) case of this.

What is new: an upper bound on the max L_{2,b} margin for b < nu that holds for every width and every kind of neuron (mixed frequencies, interference, inactive). I found no margin upper bound for modular addition under any norm other than L_{2,nu}.

recommended_citations.why: At b=nu, Thm 7 (max L_{2,3} margin sqrt(2/27)/(p^{1/2}(p-1))) is the endpoint of thm:universal. It is already in refs.bib and cited in cor:dense.
The max L_{2,k+1} margin for the power-neuron k-input sum is the b=nu endpoint of the power-neuron case.

Pricing step: L_q penalties with q<=1 written as sums of L2 penalties on multiplicative factors. The fetched page shows only the arXiv listing; the CSDA 115:186-198 journal ref comes from the sweep and I did not confirm it here.
Pricing step: l2 regularisation on parameters induces l_p/quasi-norm representation costs.

Regularisers built from the Euclidean norms of CP components are monotone transforms of the tensor Schatten-p quasi-norm. A product neuron is a rank-one CP term, so the A^{b/nu} pricing is the diagonal case.

Concurrent work. App. A.3.2 Eq 15 has the same coverage max-min with a convex l2 amplitude budget, and Prop 5 finds a dense optimum. They posit the budget for quadratic nets and give no bound over all networks, so this is a contrast to the concave b/nu budget.

chk.recommended_change: In approach.tex, after the proof of thm:universal, add: "At $b=\nu$ this is the maximum margin of \citet[Thm.~7]{morwani2024feature} and \citet{li2025fourier}; we know of no earlier margin bound for $b<\nu$ (in particular plain weight decay, $b=2$). The pricing step is the diagonal case of the fact that $\ell_2$ penalties on multiplicative factors induce $\ell_q$ quasi-norm costs \citep{hoff2017lasso,dai2021representation,fan2023euclidean}. Concurrently, \citet{kam2026symmetry} study the same coverage max-min under a convex $\ell_2$ budget on amplitudes and find the uniform (dense) allocation optimal; the concave budget $\sum_j y_j^{1/s}$ forced by homogeneity is what makes the optimum sparse." Add the new bib entries hoff2017lasso, dai2021representation, fan2023euclidean, kam2026symmetry and li2025fourier if they are missing; refs.bib currently has no Hoff, Dai, Kolb or Ongie entries.
